normalFinding.default: No palpable or tender occipital lymphadenopathy bilaterally.

steps: Face the seated patient and use the pads of your index and middle fingers.
Move the skin in small gentle circles over the base of the skull at the back on both sides together.
Note any node's size, consistency, mobility and tenderness.

normalFinding.default: Trachea midline and mobile; thyroid and cricoid cartilages non-tender.

steps: Have the patient lift the chin slightly.
Feel the thyroid and cricoid cartilages in the midline.
Check the trachea sits centrally, with equal space on each side above the sternal notch.

normalFinding.default: Thyroid not enlarged, smooth, non-tender, no nodules; rises normally on swallowing.

steps: Stand behind the seated patient with the neck in a neutral position.
Find the cricoid cartilage, then the isthmus just beneath it.
Feel each lobe while the patient swallows a sip of water, gently shifting the trachea to each side in turn.

normalFinding.default: Lids normal, conjunctivae pink, sclerae white and anicteric, irises clear.

steps: Look at lids, sclerae, conjunctivae and irises of each eye.
Ask the patient to look up while you gently draw down the lower lid.
Ask the patient to look down while you gently lift the upper lid.

normalFinding.default: Visual fields full to confrontation in all four quadrants in each eye.

steps: Sit facing the patient at eye level and have them cover one eye.
Keeping their gaze on your face, briefly show a few fingers in each quadrant and ask how many.
Repeat for the other eye.

maneuvers.label: Check pupil size and light reflexes

default.text: Pupils equal, round, 3 mm, briskly reactive to light directly and consensually.

steps: Compare pupil size and shape in dim light.
Shine the penlight straight onto one pupil and watch both pupils constrict.
Repeat on the other side.

default.text: No relative afferent pupillary defect: each pupil stays constricted as the light swings across to it.

steps: In dim light, hold the penlight on one pupil for about two seconds.
Swing the light briskly across to the other pupil, then back again.
Watch whether each pupil stays small or widens as the light arrives.

normalFinding.default: Extraocular movements full and conjugate without nystagmus or lid lag; convergence and accommodation intact.

steps: Ask the patient to keep the head still and follow your finger with the eyes only.
Trace a wide H shape through the six directions of gaze.
Bring the target in toward the nose and watch for convergence and pupil constriction.

normalFinding.default: Red reflex present; optic disc sharp with normal cup, vessels and macula unremarkable.

steps: Dim the room and ask the patient to fix on a distant point.
Use your right hand and eye for their right eye, left for left.
Approach from the side, find the red reflex, then move in close to view the disc, vessels and macula.

maneuvers.label: Otoscopic exam of ear canal and drum

normalFinding.default: Canals clear without erythema; tympanic membranes pearly grey and intact with normal landmarks and light reflex.

steps: Draw the outer ear upward and backward to straighten the canal.
Insert the speculum slowly, angled slightly forward and down.
Inspect canal, wax and drum landmarks, then repeat on the other ear.

default.text: Sound heard equally in both ears; no lateralization.

steps: Set a tuning fork vibrating.
Rest its base on the middle of the top of the head.
Ask whether the sound is louder on one side or the same in both ears.

default.text: Air conduction greater than bone conduction bilaterally.

steps: Set a tuning fork vibrating and place its base on the mastoid bone.
When the patient can no longer hear it, move the prongs next to the ear canal.
Ask whether the sound is audible again; repeat on the other side.

steps.label: Base of the fork on the mastoid (bone conduction)
Patient says the sound has stopped
Prongs beside the ear canal (air conduction)

normalFinding.default: Nasal mucosa pink and moist, septum midline, no discharge, polyps or lesions.

steps: Face the patient and gently insert a short nasal speculum or tilt the nose tip up.
Look at the lower nasal passage, then have the patient tip the head back slightly.
Check mucosa colour, septum and any lesions on each side.

normalFinding.default: Lips, mucosa and palate pink and moist; uvula midline; tonsils not enlarged; pharynx without erythema or exudate.

steps: Use a light to look at the lips, tongue, buccal mucosa, palate and parotid duct openings.
Press a tongue depressor on the back half of the tongue to view the pharynx and tonsils.
Ask the patient to say 'ah' to improve the view.

maneuvers.label: Inspect tongue and floor of mouth

normalFinding.default: Tongue moist and midline without lesions; floor of mouth without masses or lesions.

steps: Ask the patient to stick out the tongue, then lift the tip to the roof of the mouth.
Look under the tongue at the floor of the mouth for lesions or swelling.

normalFinding.default: Dentition in good repair; gums pink without swelling, bleeding or recession.

steps: Ask the patient to bite together.
Retract the lips and cheeks with a tongue depressor or gloved finger.
Look over the teeth and gum margins.
